Thanks Alex — quick notes from Legal:

1) Credit line: replace any operational claim with a neutral formulation. Proposed: "Medisync, using Redwood Inference for clinical search and inference workloads." This avoids implying regulatory certification.

2) PII check: the quote is safe as-is (no patient data), but do not include case numbers or screenshots. If translations introduce specificity, vendor must certify no PII.

3) EU translations: include a short French/German/Spanish review step by our EU POC (Rafael) to ensure we9re not introducing medical claims in local phrasing.

4) We prefer to approve the final localized copy before publication rather than full agency autonomy. So please get the translations and route final versions to Legal (me) and CS (Grace) for sign-off.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick permission: localized testimonial for EU languages & APAC notes

We9re good from CS. Two operational requests:

- Please include a short contextual blurb with each translation that clarifies the deployment (hosted vs dedicated). Example: "Deployed on Redwood Inference hosted API with data retention settings per customer agreement."
- For APAC markets, Medisync should avoid absolute performance numbers unless backed by a benchmark we own publicly; if they want latency claims we should provide the public benchmark link instead of a numeric claim.

Once translations are back, route to marketing@redwoodinference with subject line "Medisync testimonial localized - for review". We9ll take 48 hours for final sign-off.

Grace O'Connor

Hi Linh / Eileen — thanks for the quick turn. Confirming next steps so everyone has the path forward:

1) Redwood grants permission to translate and publish the supplied testimonial into German, French, Spanish, Simplified Chinese and Japanese provided:
   - The credit line uses Legal9s approved phrasing: "Medisync, using Redwood Inference for clinical search and inference workloads."
   - Translations are submitted to Redwood for final review (Marissa + Grace).
   - No PII or screenshots are included in any localized asset.

2) Operational notes:
   - For EU language versions Rafael will do a quick regional review (3 business days).
   - For APAC languages please remove explicit latency numbers; link to our public benchmark if you want to call performance.

3) Engagement model: you may proceed with GlobalWords as the translator but request a translation QA pass and a statement that no clinical claims were added. Please route final files to marketing@redwoodinference.com and cc marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com.

4) Timeline: target publication window of Dec 149620. We9ll aim to review translations by Dec 10 to accommodate that.

I'll also drop a short DocuSign approval for the quote+credit line to formalize release for PR.

Thanks everyone — cc'ing GlobalWords for scheduling.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
